summary: WebAuthn device-assertion header mangled by ingress proxy causes SSO login loop for runbook-portal
description: Issue summary: Several on-call engineers report being unable to complete SSO login into the internal runbook-portal. Okta SSO returns success but runbook-portal displays 'authentication failed' and sends users back to Okta. This began after the 2026-03-11 ingress-api config rollout. Impact: Prevents access to runbook documentation for oncall; blocked incident responses; ~12 users affected in us-east. Observed behavior: After Okta auth, browser shows repeated redirect loop; network traces show app returning 401 with 'invalid device assertion'.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Attempt login to https://runbook-portal.redwood.local using SSO in Chrome on corp network
2) Complete Okta MFA (WebAuthn) when prompted
3) Observe redirect loop and 401 from runbook-portal
4) Capture network trace and check for X-Device-Assertion header crossing ingress
logs:
auth-service: 2026-03-12T09:42:11Z WARN failed device assertion: invalid signature
identity-proxy: 2026-03-12T09:42:11Z DEBUG incoming header X-Device-Assertion: eyJhbGciOiJI...==
ingress-api: 2026-03-12T09:42:11Z DEBUG rewrite header X-Device-Assertion: eyJhbGciOiJI... (padding stripped)
runbook-portal: 2026-03-12T09:42:11Z ERROR device assertion decode error: invalid base64 padding
investigation_notes: 03/12 09:45 - Initial triage by Support (Priya): Confirmed issue coincides with ingress-api v1.4.8 rollout from 2026-03-11.
03/12 10:05 - SRE (Carlos) reproduced locally: ingress-api was removing trailing '=' characters from Base64 device assertions when proxying between auth and app.
03/12 11:20 - Identity team confirmed WebAuthn assertions must preserve exact header value; stripping padding makes signature verification fail.
03/12 13:40 - Correlated with config change 'normalize-headers=true' in ingress-api which lowercases and trims header values.
timeline: 2026-03-12 10:30 - Reproduced by SRE; hypothesis: header rewrite
2026-03-12 14:00 - Emergency rollback of normalize-headers flag on ingress-api in us-east
workaround: Rolled back ingress-api normalize-headers config in us-east; instruct affected users to clear browser cookies if still in redirect loop.
resolution: Temporary: Reverted normalize-headers flag in ingress-api for prod us-east. Permanent: identity-proxy PR to explicitly mark X-Device-Assertion as exempt from normalization and updated ingress-api to preserve Base64 headers. QA and canary passed 2026-03-13. Owner: identity team to deploy global fix.
follow_up_actions: Add integration test to ingress-api to ensure Base64 and WebAuthn headers are preserved
Update runbook-portal SSO diagnostics page to log full header presence (not values)
verification_steps: 1) Confirm users can SSO into runbook-portal in us-east; 2) Check ingress-api logs show X-Device-Assertion unchanged; 3) Run automated integration test in staging.
comments: Priya Menon (03/12 09:50): 'Multiple oncall reporting inability to access runbooks. No user-facing change documented. Escalating to SRE.'
Carlos Ruiz (03/12 10:10): 'Reproduced; ingress-api is trimming header padding. Rolling back normalize-headers in us-east now.'
Jordan Lee (Identity Eng) (03/12 11:30): 'Known issue with earlier normalize-headers behavior; we'll add an allowlist for device assertion headers in identity-proxy. Draft PR created.'
Priya Menon (03/12 14:20): 'Rollback verified by two affected users. Marking P1 resolved for us-east; leaving ticket open for permanent fix.'
Jordan Lee (03/13 09:00): 'PR merged to identity-proxy and ingress-api team accepted change. Will schedule global rollout after smoke tests.'
